newsitem.title: BRUNEI: British defence minister to visit Brunei.
newsitem.headline: British defence minister to visit Brunei.

text.p: British Defence Secretary Michael Portillo arrives in Brunei on Wednesday for talks with the sultan of this tiny oil-rich kingdom that will focus partly on the Gurkha garrison long stationed here.

Portillo and Sultan Hassanal Bolkiah, a graduate of Britain's Sandhurst military academy, will discuss the command of the Gurkha garrison once Hong Kong is handed over to China on midnight on June 30, authoritative sources said.
Brunei is also buying two frigate-class patrol boats from Britain and Portillo may discuss other defence sales, the sources said.
Britain maintains a battalion of Gurkhas in Brunei with dozens of British officers, as well as a jungle training school used by specialists such as the Special Air Service.
Hong Kong has been the command centre for the much feared British Army Gurkha force in the Far East, including the garrison in Brunei.
A battalion of Gurkhas was first stationed in Seri oilfield of the former British protectorate decades ago to protect Brunei's then sole financial asset.
The Royal Dutch/Shell group is the only oil producer in the country under a joint venture with the government.
The Gurkha force has dwindled from seven battalions at the time of Brunei's independence in 1984 to just one today. The Hong Kong handover has sparked speculation about its fate.
Portillo will also visit Hong Kong on his Asian tour.
Britain has withdrawn its Gurkha force in Hong Kong and the two remaining units are in Britain and Brunei.
British government sources said the two units would remain in place and rotate with each other every three years.
Brunei is one of several countries which claim all or part of the Spratlys, a string of islands, atolls and reefs in the South China Sea that has spawned tensions in recent years.
China and Taiwan claim all of the Spratlys, while Malaysia, Vietnam, the Philippines and Brunei claim parts of it.
